definitions_and_hypotheses_checked: Ricci flow uses the same evolving metric and its Levi-Civita connection; time derivatives are within nondegenerate intervals, including included endpoints.
Normalized data are three-dimensional, complete and finite volume; curvature <=1 and half-Euclidean calibrated ball volume hold at every center and every radius 0<r<=1.
Local existence and uniqueness use compact carriers; continuation has one global full-curvature bound for every t in [0,T) and every x, with 0<T<infinity.

Local Shi constants are chosen after n,k,K,alpha,r but before the carrier, T, flow and center; T<=alpha/K; the original ball has compact closure and curvature bounded throughout its fixed spatial cylinder.
Initial-derivative variant retains GLOBAL curvature and initial derivative bounds through l, uses natural subtraction max(k-l,0), and at t=0 requires k<=l.

Positivity preservation is compact and three-dimensional; scalar-zero rigidity is connected and three-dimensional with nonnegative sectional curvature throughout, without a completeness or compactness premise.
Hamilton-Ivey persistence uses absolute a>=0, [a,b), both scalar and logarithmic initial bounds, and the full norm convention |Rm|^2=4 sum k_i^2.

Harnack is all-dimensional and uses forall t exists K_t forall x, not a uniform time bound. The ancient public result retains connectedness and nonflatness on every slice. Time-zero derivative is one-sided.
Finite path comparison has both elapsed-time factors; paths are C1 for the actual evolving metric. No division by scalar curvature is used.
Pointed compactness has forall A>0 exists K_A eventually k forall s,t in J forall x in the s-ball. The approximants need eventual precompact zero-time balls, not globally complete metrics.

Product-flow spacetime embeddings preserving partial_t and agreeing with the identity at time zero are time independent. The extra spacetime-control field is supplied by identity maps from the retained all-time hypothesis.
Pointed limit convergence includes all mixed coordinate jets, relatively compact connected exhaustion, a strict subsequence and based embeddings; completeness is claimed at interior times only.

The bound K_t in the Harnack interface uses the ordered-pair quadratic operator convention; existence of a bound is equivalent under the usual Lambda^2 normalization. No numerical operator-bound constant is transported unchanged.

substantive_proof_mechanisms.mechanism: Parseval tensor probes and full-support L2 measure; closability by distributional integration by parts; compact dense graph inclusion j and resolvent jj*, spectral generator beta^-1-1; energy and C0-times-L2 residual splitting. Lipschitz constant 8 C1 rho + 2 C2 sqrt T; explicit rho=1/(64(C1+1)) and T=s^2; forcing norm <=rho/3; positive metric >=3g0/4; parameter-orbit spatial smoothness; pullback along -W. Uniqueness energy rates CE, CE+D/2, CE-D close with Gronwall; bounded jets yield terminal metric and smooth restart.

Clipped increasing branch joined to horizontal -3/(1+t), least-eigenvalue concavity, completed-square nonnegative reaction polynomial, transported rate-two PDE and fixed carrier after scaling, outward support/Laplacian first contact, scalar clock and ordered-spectrum norm estimate.

Tensor-square Gram contraction proves sharp reaction positivity; prescribed skew spatial jet and explicit C(n,K,T) give strict contact with alpha=epsilon exp(A tau) rho/tau and psi=delta exp(A tau). Compact normalized directions exclude first zeros. Stationary descent of truncated injectivity plus a convex exhaustion gives initial unit-ball volume. Scalar-integral input controls linear volume loss. Expanding cylinders with A=k+1, Q>[64(n+8)A]^2 and scalar<=4Q are buffered backward before extraction; resulting all-radius volume coefficient is nu/4^n. Bounded ancient zero AVR contradicts this. Chen estimate uses L=D exp(8K), absorbs exp(8K)H<=Q/2, and yields the right bound. Supremum continuation, trace and integrating factors finish.

Controlled normal charts and mixed jets; diagonal metric and distance limits; zero-distance quotient and transition cocycles; finite chart correction preserving a protected basepoint; compact source-ball cover yields escaping boundaries and zero-time completeness; transfer two-time curvature through embeddings; bounded Cauchy sequences compare locally with the complete zero-time metric.
